title: Overfitting and Generalisation
summary: Identify overfitting from a train-vs-test performance gap and describe at least one way to reduce it.
objectives: Compute the train-test gap for a model
Diagnose a model as overfit, underfit or well-generalised from its train and test accuracy
Propose one specific fix for an overfit model and one for an underfit model
Choose which model to deploy, using the test score and the diagnosis

segments.title: What you will build
segments.body:
## What you will build

Three teams trained a model on the same task and sent you their train and test accuracy. Your job is the one a reviewer does every day: look at the two numbers, work out the gap between them, and say whether each model has **overfit** (memorised the training data), **underfit** (too simple to learn the pattern) or **generalised well**. You will store the diagnosis for each model in a dictionary, suggest one concrete fix for each problem model, and name the model you would deploy. No scikit-learn is needed: this lab is about reading the numbers correctly, which is the skill you will use on every model you ever train.

lab.title: Diagnose three models
lab.objective: Use the train-test gap to diagnose three models as overfit, underfit or well-generalised, propose fixes and pick one to deploy.
lab.instructions:
The dictionary results gives, for three models, the accuracy on the training data and on the test data (as decimals: 0.99 means 99%).

Use this rule from class:
- gap = train - test, rounded to 2 decimals
- if the gap is bigger than 0.10, the model is overfit
- otherwise, if the test accuracy is below 0.70, the model is underfit
- otherwise the model is well-generalised

1. Build gaps: a dictionary from model name to its gap (rounded to 2 decimals).
2. Build diagnosis: a dictionary from model name to exactly one of the strings "overfit", "underfit" or "well-generalised".
3. Print one line per model, in the order model_a, model_b, model_c, in exactly this shape:
model_a: train 0.99, test 0.61, gap 0.38 -> <diagnosis>
4. Build fixes: a dictionary with one entry for each model that is NOT well-generalised. Each value is one specific fix of at least 5 words. For an overfit model suggest a simpler model, more training data or regularisation. For an underfit model suggest a more complex or flexible model, or adding more features.
5. Set chosen_model to the name of the model you would deploy: the best test accuracy among the models that are not overfit. Print it as the last line: Deploy: <chosen_model>
lab.constraints: Apply the rule with if/elif/else inside a loop, so the code would still work if the numbers changed. Keep the names results, gaps, diagnosis, fixes and chosen_model. Use the exact strings overfit, underfit and well-generalised. No input().
hints: Loop with for name, scores in results.items(): and compute gap = round(scores["train"] - scores["test"], 2). Store it with gaps[name] = gap.

The rule is an if/elif/else chain inside the loop: if gap > 0.10: diagnosis[name] = "overfit" elif scores["test"] < 0.70: diagnosis[name] = "underfit" else: diagnosis[name] = "well-generalised". Print the line in the same loop.

model_a is overfit and model_b is underfit, so fixes needs those two keys, e.g. fixes["model_a"] = "use a simpler model or collect more training data". The best test accuracy among the models that are not overfit belongs to model_c, so chosen_model = "model_c".

visible_examples.code:
train = 0.95
test = 0.62
gap = round(train - test, 2)
print("Gap:", gap)
if gap > 0.10:
    print("overfit")
else:
    print("not overfit")

One line per model is printed in the required shape
The Deploy: line names a model
diagnosis gives each model the right label
fixes gives a specific fix for each problem model
chosen_model is the model to deploy

tests.label: gaps holds the three rounded gaps
tests.remediation: gap = round(train - test, 2) for every model; store it in gaps under the model name (gaps[name] = gap).

tests.label: One line per model is printed in the required shape
tests.remediation: Print inside the loop: print(f"{name}: train {scores['train']}, test {scores['test']}, gap {gaps[name]} -> {diagnosis[name]}"), so there are three lines, model_a first.

definition.stdout_regex: ^model_a: train 0\.\d+, test 0\.\d+, gap 0\.\d+ -> [a-z-]+\nmodel_b: train 0\.\d+, test 0\.\d+, gap 0\.\d+ -> [a-z-]+\nmodel_c: train 0\.\d+, test 0\.\d+, gap 0\.\d+ -> [a-z-]+$

tests.label: The Deploy: line names a model
tests.remediation: Finish with print("Deploy:", chosen_model) where chosen_model is one of the model names.

tests.label: diagnosis gives each model the right label
tests.remediation: Apply the rule in order: gap > 0.10 means overfit; otherwise test < 0.70 means underfit; otherwise well-generalised. Use the exact spellings overfit, underfit and well-generalised.
tests.objective: Diagnose overfitting and underfitting from train/test scores

tests.label: fixes gives a specific fix for each problem model
tests.remediation: fixes needs exactly the keys model_a and model_b (the two models that are not well-generalised), each with a fix of at least 5 words. For the overfit model mention a simpler model, more data or regularisation; for the underfit model mention a more complex or flexible model, or more features.
tests.objective: Propose a specific fix for overfitting and underfitting

tests.label: chosen_model is the model to deploy
tests.remediation: Deploy the model with the best test accuracy among those that are not overfit. Compare the test scores, not the train scores.
